components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Tactile, chunky, and undeniable action button.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--color-primary-container, #d6ff00); color: var(--color-neutral-text, #1c1b1b); padding: 16px 24px; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.5px; text-transform: uppercase; border: 3px solid #1c1b1b; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 0 #1c1b1b; transition: transform 0.1s, box-shadow 0.1s; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translate(4px, 4px); box-shadow: 0px 0px 0 0 #1c1b1b; }

narrative.overview: ShuttleShuffle is designed to be unapologetically bold, highly legible, and deeply tactile. Drawing from the brand personality of a 'Playful Neo-Brutalist', the system relies on stark contrasts, thick strokes, and solid, un-blurred shadows to create a UI that acts as both an organizer and a referee. The aesthetic is energetic but unpretentious, prioritizing extreme clarity from a distance—as it often acts as a physical scoreboard placed at the back of a badminton court. It explicitly rejects fragile glassmorphism, low-contrast SaaS clichés, and over-designed decoration that doesn't serve the game.
keyCharacteristics: Physical, tactile interactions driven by solid neo-brutalist shadows.
Distinct boundaries built with thick, deliberate strokes.
Function over decoration; everything serves to clarify the match state.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The High-Visibility Volt (#d6ff00) is the loudest voice on the court. It must be reserved for the most important action or state on the screen.

rules.name: The Monumental Score Rule
rules.body: Score numbers must be rendered in Bricolage Grotesque ExtraBold at sizes ranging from 80px to 120px. They are not just text; they are graphic elements.

rules.name: The Flat-Blur Rule
rules.body: All shadows are solid blocks. Blur is explicitly set to 0. A surface is either flush with the background or physically hoisted above it by a solid shape.

dos: Do use thick (3px) and thin (1.5px) borders to define component boundaries clearly.
Do ensure interactive elements translate physically when pressed, matching their shadow offset.
Do use uppercase Space Grotesk for utility labels and buttons to maintain a technical, scoreboard-like feel.
donts: Don't use corporate, overly formal, or bland SaaS designs.
Don't use over-designed complex UI that is hard to read from a distance.
Don't use fragile glassmorphism, semi-transparent layers, or blurred shadows that reduce legibility.
Don't make touch targets smaller than 48px; users will be interacting with the app during active games.
